problems.name: Two Sum
problems.question: Given an integer array nums and an integer target, return the indexes of two distinct elements whose values add up to target. If no pair exists, return {-1, -1}.
problems.constraints: 2 <= nums.length <= 10^4; -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; -10^9 <= target <= 10^9; indexes must be distinct.

examples.explanation: The same value can be used twice only when it appears at two different indexes.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n).

problems.name: Contains Duplicate
problems.question: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice. Return false if every element is distinct.

examples.explanation: The value 1 appears at indexes 0 and 3.
Every value appears exactly once.
Multiple values appear more than once.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n).

problems.name: Valid Anagram
problems.question: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s. Return false otherwise. Both strings contain lowercase English letters.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 5 * 10^4; s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Both strings contain the same letters with the same frequencies.
The character counts are different.
s has two a characters, but t has only one.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1) because the frequency array has fixed size 26.

problems.name: Group Anagrams
problems.question: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You may return the groups in any order.
problems.constraints: 1 <= strs.length <= 10^4; 0 <= strs[i].length <= 100; strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: eat, tea, and ate share one signature; tan and nat share another; bat is alone.
The empty string forms one valid group.
A single word is grouped by itself.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * k), Space O(n * k), because each word builds a 26-count key and is stored in a hash map group.

problems.name: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.question: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. The answer may be returned in any order.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5; -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4; k is in [1, number of unique elements]; answer is guaranteed unique as a set.

examples.explanation: 1 appears 3 times and 2 appears 2 times.
The only element is also the most frequent.
4 has the highest frequency.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n), using frequency buckets from 1 to n.

problems.name: Product of Array Except Self
problems.question: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer where answer[i] equals the product of all elements of nums except nums[i]. Solve it in O(n) time without using division.
problems.constraints: 2 <= nums.length <= 10^5; -30 <= nums[i] <= 30; products fit in 32-bit integer; division is not allowed.

examples.explanation: For index 0, product is 2 * 3 * 4 = 24; for index 1, product is 1 * 3 * 4 = 12.
Only the index containing 0 gets the product of all non-zero values.
Each answer is the other element.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1) excluding the output array.

source.label: LeetCode 238 - Product of Array Except Self

problems.name: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.question: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the total number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose sum equals k.

examples.explanation: The valid subarrays are nums[0..1] and nums[1..2].
The valid subarrays are [1,2] and [3].
The valid subarray is nums[1..2] = [-1,1].

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n), using a hash map of prefix-sum frequencies.

problems.name: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.question: Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence. The optimized solution must run in O(n) time.
problems.constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 10^5; -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; optimized solution should be O(n).

examples.explanation: The longest consecutive sequence is [1,2,3,4].
The longest sequence is [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8].
No elements means no consecutive sequence.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n), because each number is expanded at most once from a sequence head.

problems.name: Majority Element
problems.question: Given an integer array nums, return the majority element. The majority element appears more than floor(n / 2) times, and it is guaranteed to exist.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 5 * 10^4; -2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; majority element always exists.

examples.explanation: 3 appears 2 times, which is more than floor(3 / 2).
2 appears 4 times, which is more than floor(7 / 2).
The only element is the majority element.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1), using Boyer-Moore voting.

problems.name: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
problems.question: Given an integer array nums of length n where every nums[i] is in the range [1, n], return all numbers in the range [1, n] that do not appear in nums.
problems.constraints: n == nums.length; 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= nums[i] <= n.

examples.explanation: The numbers 5 and 6 from range [1,8] do not appear.
The value 2 is missing from range [1,2].
Every number from 1 to 4 appears.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1) excluding the output list, using in-place marking.

source.label: LeetCode 448 - Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array

problems.name: Intersection of Two Arrays
problems.question: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, return an array of their intersection. Each element in the result must be unique, and the result may be returned in any order.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums1.length, nums2.length <= 1000; 0 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 1000; each output value must be unique.

examples.explanation: 2 appears in both arrays, but output values must be unique.
Both 9 and 4 appear in both arrays; order does not matter.
There are no common values.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(m + n), Space O(m + r), where r is the number of unique intersection values.

problems.name: First Unique Character in a String
problems.question: Given a string s, find the first non-repeating character and return its index. If it does not exist, return -1.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 10^5; s consists of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: l is the first character that appears once.
v at index 2 is the first non-repeating character.
Every character appears more than once.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1), because the count array has fixed size 26.

problems.name: Encode and Decode Strings

problems.constraints: Design problem; encode and decode must be inverse operations for arbitrary strings.

examples.explanation: Decoding restores the original list.
An empty string is encoded as length 0.
The delimiter is safe because length controls parsing.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(totalChars), Space O(totalChars), using length-prefix encoding.
